title: C482/388/2022 of RAJENDRA SINGH YADAV Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No. 388 of 2022
Rajendra Singh Yadav and others .......Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and another ........ Respondents
Present : Mr. Gaurav Singh, Advocate for the petitioner appeared through
video conferencing.
 Mr. Dinesh Chauhan and Mr. P.S. Uniyal, Brief Holders for the
State/respondent no.1.
 Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate for respondent no.2.

JUDGMENT
Per : Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
The challenge in this revision is made to the
judgment and order dated 04.03.2022, passed in
Criminal Revision No. 496 of 2018, Smt. Urmila vs. State
of Uttarakhand and others, by the court of 1st Additional
Sessions Judge, Roorkee, District Haridwar ("the
revision"). By which, the revision was allowed and the
court below was directed to hear the matter afresh.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. The private respondent filed an application
under Section 156 (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (for short, "the Code"). Based on which, the
proceeding of Criminal Case No.188 of 2018, Smt. Urmila

2
vs. Rajendra and others was instituted in the court of
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Roorkee, District
Haridwar, which was rejected on 05.07.2018. This order
was challenged in the revision, by which, the revision was
allowed and the court below was directed to hear the case
under Section 156(3) of the Code afresh.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionists had taken
a ground that in the revision, they were not served with
the notice. Without hearing them the order has been
passed.
5. Learned counsel for the private respondent
would submit that notice could not be served on the
revisionists, therefore, he would also submit that the
impugned order may be set aside and the matter be
remanded to the revision court to hear the revision afresh
after affording the opportunity of hearing.
6. Since, it is admitted that the revisionists were
not heard in the revision. Therefore, the impugned
judgment and order 04.03.2022 is set aside. The
revisional court shall hear the Criminal Revision
No. 496 of 2018 afresh after affording an

3
opportunity of hearing to the parties. The revisionists
should not be issued any fresh notice in the revision.
7. Learned counsel for the revisionists gives a
statement that they would appear in the court of 1st
Additional Sessions Judge, Roorkee, District Haridwar on
15.05.2023.
8. The parties shall appear in the court below on
15.05.2023.
9. With the observation as above, the petition is
disposed of.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 03.04.2023
Sanjay
